 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__****⇒ Sugarcane contains Glucose + Fructose.**

 
• Fructose is a monosaccharide.
 
• A monosaccharide is the simplest form of sugar and the smallest unit of carbohydrate which cannot be further divided.
 
• When two monosaccharides join it forms a molecule called Disaccharide.
 
• All the other options are disaccharides

 
 

 
 
Glucose + Fructose

 
 
 
Sucrose(Found in Sugarcane)

 
 
 

 
 
Glucose + Glucose

 
 
 
Maltose

 
 
 

 
 
Glucose + Galactose

 
 
 
Lactose(Found in Milk)

 
 
 

 

 
• Honey Bee is a colonial insect living in beehives consisting of one queen (a fertile female), a few drones (males), and thousands of workers (infertile females).
 
• Around 5 to 25% of the workers are scouts whose job is to search for a new source of food while the foragers harvest food. 
 
• When the food is within 50 to 75 meters of the hive the Scouts perform a round dance. 
 
• Whereas if the food is farther than 75 meters from the hive the Scout's dance is called the waggle dance.

question: At the end of a conference, all the 30 people present shake hands with each other once. How many handshakes will there be altogether?
solution:
Number of people in the conference = 30

Each person shakes hands with others.

**Concept used:**

When n people shake hands with each other, the total number of handshakes = ⁿC₂

**Calculation:**

Total number of handshakes = ³⁰C₂ = (30 × 29)/2 = 870/2 = 435 handshakes.

**Hence,**** The total number of handshakes is 435.**

subject: REAS
question: The sum of four numbers A, B, C and D is 147. The ratio of C and D is 3 ∶ 5, respectively. D is five times A. C is twice of B. What is the value of B ?
solution:
Given:

1) A, B, C and D is 147

**=> A + B + C +D = 147 --------- (i)**

2) The ratio of C and D is 3 ∶ 5.

=> C : D = 3 : 5

Let the common factor between C and D is ‘x’

**So, C = 3x; and D = 5x ****--------- (ii)**

3) D is five times A. C is twice of B.

=> D = 5A and C = 2B

Putting the value of C and D from eq. (ii)

=> 5x = 5A and 3x = 2B

**=> A = x and B = 1.5x** **---------- (iii)**

Putting the value of A and B from eq. (iii) and C and D from eq. (ii) in eq (i)

=> x + 1.5x + 3x + 5x = 147

=> 10.5x = 147

=> x = 147 ÷ 10.5

=> x = 14

Since B = 1.5x

So, B = 1.5 × 14 = 21

Hence, The value of B is **“21”.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

1) A, B, C and D is 147

=> A + B + C +D = 147 --------- (i)

2) The ratio of C and D is 3 ∶ 5.

=> C : D = 3 : 5

3) D is five times A. C is twice of B.

=> D = 5A and C = 2B

=> D : A = 5 : 1 and C : B = 2 :1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/919cc88eddfcd603612f3a5a9a4208a65dbd01ce11df519e28f6cd897eca69b6.png] 

Hence, The value of B is “21”.

question: The total of the salary of Mandeep and Swati is ₹85,000. The total of the salary of Swati and Yukti is ₹60,000. If Swati's salary is ₹10,000 more than the salary of Yukti, then what is the salary of Mandeep?
solution:
Given:

**1) The total of the salary of Mandeep and Swati is ₹85,000.**

=> Mandeep + Swati = 85,000 ------------ (i)

**2) The total of the salary of Swati and Yukti is ₹60,000.**

=> Swati + Yukti = 60,000 ------------ (ii)

**3) Swati's salary is ₹10,000 more than the salary of Yukti.**

=> Swati = 10000 + Yukti

=> Yukti = Swati - 10000

**Putting this value in equation (ii)**

=> Swati + Swati - 10000= 60000

=> 2 × Swati = 60000 + 10000

=> Swati = 70000 ÷ 2

=> Swati = 35000

**Putting the salary of Swati in eq. (i)**

=> Mandeep + 35000 = 85,000

=> Mandeep = 85000 – 35000

=> Mandeep = 50000

Hence, The salary of Mandeep is **“50000”.**85:T97

subject: REAS
question:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

12 - 14 × 21 ÷ 7 + 28 = 193
solution:
By using BODMAS RULE :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3a84c2624712eb918bcca3c6fa1b16dca3d9cacbb6fc6d03a6c4e496059d1a05.png] 

Option 1) : × and -

Given equation is : 12 - 14 × 21 ÷ 7 + 28 = 193 

After interchanging the symbols the equation formed is : 

⇒ 12 × 14 - __**21 ÷ 7**__ + 28 = 193

⇒ __**12 × 14**__ - 3 + 28 = 193

⇒ __**168**__ - 3 __**+ 28**__ = 193

⇒ **__196 - 3__** = 193

**⇒ 193 = 193**

**LHS = RHS**

Option 2) : + and ×

Given equation is : 12 - 14 × 21 ÷ 7 + 28 = 193 

After interchanging the symbols the equation formed is : 

⇒ 12 - 14 + **__21 ÷ 7__** × 28 = 193

⇒ 12 - 14 + **__3 × 28__** = 193

⇒ __**12**__ - 14 **__+ 84__** = 193

⇒ **__96__****__ - 14__** = 193

⇒ 82 ≠ 193

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) : + and ÷

Given equation is : 12 - 14 × 21 ÷ 7 + 28 = 193 

After interchanging the symbols the equation formed is :

⇒ 12 - 14 × 21 + **__7 ÷ 28__** = 193

⇒ 12 - **__14 × 21__** + 0.25 = 193

⇒ __**12**__ - 294 **__+ 0.25__** = 193

⇒ **__12.25 - 294__** = 193

⇒ - 281.75 ≠ 193

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) : × and ÷

Given equation is : 12 - 14 × 21 ÷ 7 + 28 = 193 

After interchanging the symbols the equation formed is : 

⇒ 12 - **__14 ÷ 21__** × 7 + 28 = 193

⇒ 12 - __**0.66 × 7**__ + 28 = 193

⇒ __**12**__ - 4.66 **__+ 28__** = 193

⇒ __**40**____** - 4.66**__ = 193

⇒ 35.33 ≠ 193

LHS ≠ RHS

question: An amount of Rs. 1,189 is to be divided among Rakesh, Mrinal and Sanjay in the ratio of 11 : 13 : 17, respectively. How much amount will Sanjay get more than Rakesh?
solution:
Total amount = Rs. 1,189

Total amount divided among Rakesh, Mrinal, Sanjay is in ratio of = 11 : 13 : 17

Total amount divided into number of parts = 11 + 13 + 17 = 41 parts

∴ 41 parts = Rs. 1,189

⇒ 1 part = 1189 ÷ 41

⇒ 1 part = Rs. 29

Number of parts Sanjay received = 17 parts

Amount of Sanjay got = 17 × 29 = 493/-

Number of parts Rakesh received = 11 parts

Amount of Rakesh = 11 × 29 = 319

Amount of Sanjay got more than Rakesh = 493 - 319 = 174/-

Hence, the correct answer is **"174".**

question: If the ratio of the present ages of Shikha and Rajkumar is 2 ∶ 1, and 15 years ago the ratio of their ages was 3 ∶ 1, then the present age (in years) of Shikha is:
solution:
Given, Ratio of present ages of Shikha and Rajkumar = 2 :1

Let us consider present ages of Shikha and Rajkumar = 2x : x

15 years ago the ratio of their ages was = 3 ∶ 1

Hence,

(2x - 15) / (x - 15) = 3 / 1

2x - 15 = 3(x - 15)

2x - 15 = 3x - 45

3x - 2x = 45 - 15

∴ x = 30

Thus, the present age of Shikha = 2x = 2 × 30 = 60 years

Hence, the correct answer is **"60".**

question: Presently Suman is four times as old as her son. Five years ago, she was seven times as old as her son. What is the age of her son?
solution:
Given: Suman is four times as old as her son. Five years ago, she was seven times as old as her son. 

Let the present age or Suman be 'S' and that of her son be 'p'.

According to the question,

S = 4 × p -----------(i)

S - 5 = 7 × (p - 5)

Putting the value of S from equ. (i);

4p - 5 = 7p - 35

7p - 4p = 35 - 5

3p = 30

**p = 10**

Hence, the age of the son of Suman is **10 years.**

subject: REAS
question: The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 58 years. Four years ago, the ratio of their ages was 4 : 1. What is the present age of the father?
solution:
** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Given: 

The present ages of a father and his son = 58 years 

Four years ago, the ratio of their ages = 4 : 1.

**Calculation:**

Let the present age of a father be (4x + 4) and the present age of a son be (x + 4)

According to the question,

The present age of a father and his son = 58 years 

⇒ (4x + 4) + (x + 4) = 58

⇒ 5x + 8 = 58

⇒ 5x = 50

⇒ x = 10

The present age of a father = (4x + 4) = 44 years

**∴ The present age of a father is 44 years.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** The logic followed here is :-

Sum of present ages of father and son = 58 years

Father + Son = 58 years .............. (i)

The ratio of ages 4 years ago is = 4 : 1

⇒ (Father - 4) / (Son - 4) = 4 / 1

⇒ Father - 4 = 4 × (Son - 4)

⇒ Father - 4 = 4Son - 16

⇒ Father = 4Son - 16 + 4

⇒ Father = 4Son - 12 ........... (ii)

By substituting equation (ii) in equation (i) we get,

⇒ 4Son - 12 + Son = 58

⇒ 5Son - 12 = 58

⇒ 5Son = 70

⇒ Son = 14

∴ Age of son = 14 years

∴ Age of Father = 58 - 14 = 44 years.

Hence, the correct answer is "44 years ".

question: A soap costs ₹7 and a pen costs ₹5. Rajesh spent ₹38 and purchased both the things. What was the number of soaps he purchased?
solution:
Let the number of soaps and pens be x and y.

Given:

A soap costs ₹7 and a pen costs ₹5. Rajesh spent ₹38 and purchased both the things.

=> 7x + 5y = 38

=> 5y = 38 - 7x

=> y = (38 − 7x) ÷ 5

**“y” should be whole number only when (38 - 7x) is divisible by 5.**

**This happens when x = 4**

Hence, the number of soaps he purchased is “4”

question: Rajan’s family spends 60% of their monthly income on groceries, 12% of their monthly income on room rent, 8% of their monthly income on medical expenses, and the remaining amount of ₹18,000 is savings. What is Rajan's family’s monthly income?
solution:
Let us consider total **monthly income of Rajan's family = 100%**

 ♦ Rajan's family spent monthly income on groceries = 60%

 ♦ Rajan's family spent monthly income on room rent = 12%

 ♦ Rajan's family spent monthly income on medical expenses = 8%

Total expenditure = 60% + 12% + 8%

Total expenditure = 80%

 ♦ **Total Income = Total Expenditure + Savings**

100% = 80% + Savings

 ♦ **Savings = 20% of Rajan's monthly income.**

Given amount of savings = 18000/-

∴ 20% = 18000/-

⇒ 1% = 18000/20

⇒ 1% = 900/-

Total monthly income of Rajan's family = 100%

As 1% = 900/- 

⇒ 1% × 100 = 900 × 100

**⇒ 100% = 90,000/-**

∴ Here, Total monthly income of Rajan's family is 90,000/-.

Hence, the correct answer is **"90,000/-".**

solution:
The logic followed here is :-

**Second number = (First number × Third number) × |Difference of first and third number|**

(7, 308, 11) → (7 × 11) × |7 - 11| = 77 × 4 = 308

Similarly,

(12, 324, 9) → (12 × 9) × |12 - 9| = 108 × 3 = 324

Hence, the correct answer is **"(12, 324, 9)".**

question: In a row, Mansi is 29th from the left and 33rd from the right. How many students are there in the row?
solution:
The logic followed here is:-

In a row, Mansi is 29th from the left and 33rd from the right.

**Total number of students in a row= (Mansi rank from the left + Rank from the right) - 1**

Number of students in row = (29 + 33) - 1

Number of students in row = 62 - 1

∴ Number of students in row = 61

Hence, the correct answer is **"61".**

question: In a class of 72 students, the number of boys is twice the number of girls. Find the number of boys.
solution:
Given number of students in class = 72

Boys = B, Girls = G

The number of boys is twice the number of girls.

B = 2G

B + G = 72

2G + G = 72

3G = 72

G = 24

∴ B = 2G

B = 2 × 24

B = 48

∴ Here, number of boys in class are '48'.

Hence, the correct answer is **"48".**

H _ S _ _ P S _ _ P _ C
solution:
Given : H _ S _ _ P S _ _ P _ C

By checking options:

1) SCHCHS ⇒ H __**S**__ S __**C**__ __**H**__ P S __**C**__ __**H**__ P __**S**__ C → (It doesn't Follows the pattern)

2) PCHHCS ⇒ H **__P__** S __C__ __H__ P S **__H__** **__C__** P __S__ C → (It doesn't Follows the pattern)

3) PHCCHS ⇒ H **__P__** S **__H__** **__C__** P S __C__ __H__ P __S__ C → (It doesn't Follows the pattern) 

4) PCHCHS ⇒ H **__P__** S __C__ / __H__ P S __C__ / __H__ P __S__ C → **(It does Follows the pattern of H P S C - H P S C - H P S C)**

Option (4) Give a pattern of H __P__ S __C__ - __H__ P S __C__ - __H__ P __S__ C

Hence, the correct answer is **"PCHCHS****"**.

question: When 12 is added to a number, it is equal to 2 times the sum of 4 and the number. Find the number.
solution:
Given,

When 12 is added to a number, it is equal to 2 times the sum of 4 and the number.

Let us consider the number = X

⇒ X + 12 = 2(X + 4)

⇒ X + 12 = 2X + 8

⇒ 2X - X = 12 - 8

∴ X = 4

So, the number X = 4

Hence, the correct answer is "4".

question: When a natural number X is added to its next natural number Y and another natural number that is five times its next natural number Y, the sum of these three numbers is 104. Find the number X.
solution:
Given,

When a natural number X is added to its next natural number Y and another natural number that is five times its next natural number Y.

First natural number = X

Next natural number Y = X + 1

Another natural number that is five times its next natural number Y = 5(X + 1)

Sum of these three numbers = 104

⇒ X + X + 1 + 5(X + 1) = 104

⇒ X + X + 1 + 5X + 5 = 104

⇒ 7X + 6 = 104

⇒ 7X = 98

**⇒ X = 14**

Hence, the correct answer is **
"14".**

question:
Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

63 ÷ 21 – 7 + 28 × 3 = 144
solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e50723751bca1df33fc1f030f78c1eac3344f2cdb432474cd432c6df783a12ab.png] 

Option 1) : + and ÷

Given equation : 63 ÷ 21 – 7 + 28 × 3 = 144 

After interchanging the symbols in given equation the equation formed is as follows : 63 + 21 - 7 ÷ 28 × 3 = 144

⇒ 63 + 21 - __**7 ÷ 28**__ × 3 = 144

⇒ 63 + 21 - __**0.25 × 3**__ = 144

⇒ __**63 + 21**__ - 0.75 = 144

⇒ __**84**____** - 0.75**__ = 144

⇒ 83.25 ≠ 144

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) : × and +

Given equation : 63 ÷ 21 – 7 + 28 × 3 = 144 

After interchanging the symbols in given equation the equation formed is as follows : 63 ÷ 21 - 7 × 28 + 3 = 144

⇒ __**63 ÷ 21**__ - 7 × 28 + 3 = 144

⇒ 3 - __**7 × 28**__ + 3 = 144

⇒ __**3**__ - 196 __**+ 3**__ = 144

⇒ __**6**____** - 196**__ = 144

⇒ - 190 ≠ 144

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 3) : ÷ and –

Given equation : 63 ÷ 21 – 7 + 28 × 3 = 144 

After interchanging the symbols in given equation the equation formed is as follows : 63 - 21 ÷ 7 + 28 × 3 = 144

⇒ 63 - __**21 ÷ 7**__ + 28 × 3 = 144

⇒ 63 - 3 + __**28 × 3**__ = 144

⇒ __**63**__ - 3 __**+ 84**__ = 144

⇒ __**147 - 3**__ = 144

⇒ **144 = 144**

**LHS = RHS**

Option 4) : + and –

Given equation : 63 ÷ 21 – 7 + 28 × 3 = 144 

After interchanging the symbols in given equation the equation formed is as follows : 63 ÷ 21 + 7 - 28 × 3 = 144

⇒ __**63 ÷ 21**__ + 7 - 28 × 3 = 144

⇒ 3 + 7 - __**28 × 3**__ = 144

⇒ __**3 + 7**__ - 84 = 144

⇒ __**10 - 84**__ = 144

⇒ - 74 ≠ 144

LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is **"÷ and –".**

question: The age of Anuj's grandfather is 4 times the age of Anuj. Anuj's grandmother is 5 years younger than his grandfather. The total of age of Anuj's grandmother and grandfather is 107 years. What is the age of Anuj?
solution:
Given,

The age of Anuj's grandfather is 4 times the age of Anuj.

Let us consider age of Anuj = X

Age of Anuj's grandfather is 4 times the age of Anuj.

Age of Anuj's grand father = 4X

Anuj's grandmother is 5 years younger than his grandfather.

Age of Anju's grand mother = 4X - 5

The total of age of Anuj's grandmother and grandfather is 107 years.

⇒ (4X - 5) + 4X = 107

⇒ 8X - 5 = 107

⇒ 8X = 112

⇒ X = 14

**∴ Here, the age of Anuj is X = 14 years.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"14 years".**

question: Sarayu bought two refrigerators at two different prices, for a total cost of ₹80,000. By selling one for 3/4 of its cost price and another for 4/3 of its cost price, she earns a profit of ₹8,000 on the whole transaction. Find the cost price of the refrigerator which was bought at a higher price.
solution:
**Given: **

The total cost price of two different refrigerators is 80,000.

The selling price of two different refrigerators is 88,000.

**Let,**

the cost price of two different refrigerators is x and y respectively.

So, x + y = 80,000 ---------------(i)

By selling one for 3/4 of its cost price and another for 4/3 of its cost price, she earns a profit of ₹8,000.

So, The selling price of two different refrigerators is 88,000. 

Therefore,

(3/4)x + (4/3)y = 88,000 

⇒ (9x + 16y)/ 12 = 88,000

⇒ 9x + 16y = 1056000 ----------------(ii)

From, (i) and (ii) 

(9x + 16y) - (9x + 9y) = 1056000 - 720000

⇒ 9x + 16y - 9x - 9y = 336000

⇒ 7y = 336000

⇒ y = 48000

Then x = 80000 - 48000 = 32000

Hence, the cost price of the refrigerator which was bought at a higher price is 48000 rs.

Hence, the correct answer is **"option (3)".**

question: The sum of five consecutive multiples of 7 is 455. What is the largest number in this series?
solution:
Given : The sum of five consecutive multiples of 7 is 455.

Explanation :

Let the five consecutive multiple of 7 be = 7X, (7X + 7), (7X + 14), (7X + 21) and (7X + 28)

Where, X is a natural number.

So, according to the question :-

 7X + (7X + 7) + (7X + 14) + (7X + 21) + (7X + 28) = 455

35X + 70 = 455

35X = 455 - 70

35X = 385

**X=11**

Therefore, by the putting the value of 'X' the five consecutive multiples of 7 will be :-

 
• 7X → (7 x 11) = 77
 
• (7X + 7) → [(7 x 11)] + 7 = 84
 
• (7X + 14) → [(7 x 11)] + 14 = 91
 
• (7X + 21) → [(7 x 11)] + 21 = 98
 
• (7X + 28) → [(7 x 11)] + 28 = **105​**

**​**Thus, 105 is the largest number in the series.

Hence, **"105"** is the correct answer.

subject: REAS
question: When a number is added to its previous number and another number that is two times its previous number, the sum of these three numbers is 61. Find the number.
solution:
Let the number be 'a'.

According to question:

a + (a - 1) + 2(a - 1) = 61

⇒ a + a - 1 + 2a - 2 = 61

⇒ 4a - 3 = 61

⇒ 4a = 61 + 3

⇒ 4a = 64

⇒ a = 64 ÷ 4

⇒ a = 16

Hence, '**16**' is the correct answer.

E_ _CD _ H J _ _ E H _ _ D

options.text: H, E, C, D, C, J, C
H, J, C, E, C, E, H
H, J, E, C, D, J, C
H, C, E, J, D, C, E

• H, E, C, D, C, J, C → E **H E **C D - **C** H J **D C** - E H **J C** D

Hence, '**H, J, E, C, D, J, C**' is the correct answer.

question: The sum of three numbers A, B and C is 187. B is 1.5 times of A. C is twice of B. What is the value of C?
solution:
The sum of three numbers A, B and C is 187. 

A + B + C = 187 ______ (i)

B is 1.5 times of A. 

B = 1.5 × A

⇒ B ÷ 1.5 = A ______ (ii)

C is twice of B. 

C = 2B ______ (iii)

Substituting the value of (ii) and (iii) in (i), we get:

B ÷ 1.5 + B + 2B = 187

⇒ (B + 1.5B + 3B) ÷ 1.5 = 187

⇒ 5.5B = 187 × 1.5

⇒ 5.5B = 280.5

⇒ B = 280.5 ÷ 5.5

⇒ B = 51

C = 2B = 2 × 51 = 102

So, the value of C is 102.

Hence, '**102**' is the correct answer.

question: Ramesh has an equal number of coins of one-rupee, five-rupee and ten-rupee. He has a total of ₹640. How many total coins does he have?
solution:
Let us assume that Ramesh has 'a' number of equal coins.

According to question:

1a + 5a + 10a = 640

⇒ 16a = 640

⇒ a = 640 ÷ 16

⇒ a = 40

Therefore, total number of coins that Ramesh have = 3a = 3 × 40 = 120

Hence, '**120**' is the correct answer.

solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic:** In a column: (2nd number - 3rd number) ÷ 2 = 1st number

solution:

**Square (Square root of first number + **Square root of second number** )² = Third number **

So,

 
• First column

({ sqrt{25}} + { sqrt{36}})² = 121

(5 + 6)² = 121

(11)² = 121

121 = 121 (LHS = RHS)

 
• Second column

({ sqrt{49}} + { sqrt{64}})² = 225

(7 + 8)² = 225

(15)² = 225

225 = 225 (LHS = RHS)

Similarly,

 
• Third column 

({ sqrt{144}} + { sqrt{196}})² = ?

(12 + 14)² = ?

(26)² = ?

**? = 676**

Hence, **"676"** is the correct answer.

question: A class has a total of 30 students. Aaditya is at 11th rank in merit order from the top. What is the rank of Aaditya from the bottom?
solution:
Given,

Total number of students in class = 30

 Aaditya is at 11th rank in merit order from the top.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/739380da42eefafd7caa88da5805a90355979cf55a3e42da25fe9f982de11d2b.png] 

The Rank of Aaditya from bottom = Number of students in class - Aaditya rank from top + 1

The Rank of Aaditya from bottom = 30 - 11 + 1

The Rank of Aaditya from bottom = 31 - 11

The Rank of Aaditya from bottom = 20

∴ Here, the Rank of Aaditya from bottom is 20th.

Hence, the correct answer is **"20th".**

question:
Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series.

Q _ T J _ Q R _ J C _ R T _ C Q _ T _ C

options.text: R C J Q J R R
R C Q T J R J
R C T Q J R J
C R T Q J R J

solution:
Given :- Q _ T J _ Q R _ J C _ R T _ C Q _ T _ C

By checking options and substituting accordingly.

1) R C J Q J R R → Q **R** T J **C** - Q R **J** J C - **Q** R T **J** C - Q **R** T **R** C

2) R C Q T J R J → Q **R** T J **C** - Q R **Q** J C - **T** R T **J** C - Q **R** T **J** C

3) R C T Q J R J → Q **R** T J **C** - Q R **T** J C - **Q** R T **J** C - Q **R** T **J** C

 
• Here **"QRTJC"** is repeated.

4) C R T Q J R J → Q **C** T J **R** - Q R **T** J C - **Q** R T **J** C - Q **R** T **J** C

 
• Option (3) gives the pattern of :- Q R T J C - Q R T J C - Q R T J C - Q R T J C

Hence, the correct answer is **"R C T Q J R J".**

question: When a number is added to thrice its preceding number, and the sum of these two numbers is divided by 5, 13 is obtained as the result. Find that number.
solution:
Given,

The number is added to thrice its preceding number.

Let us consider number = X

The other number is = 3(X - 1)

The sum of these two numbers is divided by 5, 13

⇒ (X + 3(X - 1) ) ÷ 5 × 13 = 1

⇒ X + 3X - 3 = 65

⇒ 4X - 3 = 65

⇒ 4X = 68

⇒** X = 17**

Hence, the correct answer is **"17".**

question: In a certain code language, PLACARD is coded as 29-3-23, and DORMATS is coded as 37-13-40. How will CONFUSE be coded in that language?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b1ef5af07dc7cdface0347994bbc6f824cbda2bac27bcab0cb4cf07968dfa00.png] 

The logic followed here is :-

**Sum of first three alphabet positional value - Fourth alphabet positional value - Sum of last three alphabet positional value.**

PLACARD is coded as 29-3-23.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f38749b37fd50982ef31971df09b059353b2270a8990c446de9208348572cf0c.png] 

= (16 + 12 + 1) - 3 - (1 + 18 + 4)

= 29-3-23

And

DORMATS is coded as 37-13-40.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/353aa86bb9b1dd06c335abebebb95f8573e5ebb9a1e53111a6fb9320af3b7116.png] 

= (4 + 15 + 18) - 13 - (1 + 20 + 19)

= 37-13-40

Similarly,

CONFUSE will be coded as :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f702d7ffffa089b193a25f1a768cdc8e74ee536fa99bf3804faf0a5a466121d6.png] 

**= (3 + 15 + 14) - 6 - (21 + 19 + 5)**

**= 32-6-45**

Hence, the correct answer is **"32-6-45".**

M Y A A Y A Y
Y M A Q Y A M
M Y A Q Y A M

solution:

By checking options and substituting accordingly.

1) M A Y Y Q M A → A Y **M** Q - A **A** M Q - **Y** Y M **Y** - A **Q** M Q - **M** Y **Q** Q

2) M Y A A Y A Y → A Y **M** Q - A **Y** M Q - **A** Y M **A** - A **Y** M Q - **A** Y **Y **Q

3) Y M A Q Y A M → A Y **Y** Q - A **M** M Q - **A** Y M **Q** - A **Y** M Q - **A** Y **M **Q

4) M Y A Q Y A M → A Y **M** Q - A **Y** M Q - **A** Y M **Q - **A **Y** M Q - **A** Y **M** Q

 
• Here, **"AYMQ"** is repeated.
 
• Option (4) gives the pattern of :- A Y M Q - A Y M Q - A Y M Q - A Y M Q - A Y M Q.

question:
Which two mathematical signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct?

106 ÷ 3 × 2 + 70 – 7 = 110
solution:
The logic followed here is :-

By using BODMAS RULE.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e50723751bca1df33fc1f030f78c1eac3344f2cdb432474cd432c6df783a12ab.png] 

Option 1) : × and –

Given equation : 106 ÷ 3 × 2 + 70 – 7 = 110

After interchanging the symbols in given equation is as follows : 106 ÷ 3 - 2 + 70 × 7 = 110

⇒ __**106 ÷ 3**__ - 2 + 70 × 7 = 110

⇒ 35.33 - 2 + __**70 × 7**__ = 110

⇒ __**35.33**__ - 2 + __**490**__ = 110

⇒ __**525.33 - 2**__ = 110

⇒ 523.33 ≠ 110

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 2) : – and ÷

Given equation : 106 ÷ 3 × 2 + 70 – 7 = 110

After interchanging the symbols in given equation is as follows :

 

106 - 3 × 2 + 70 ÷ 7 = 110

⇒ 106 - 3 × 2 + __**70 ÷ 7**__ = 110

⇒ 106 - __**3 × 2**__ + 10 = 110

⇒ __**106**__ - 6 __**+ 10**__ = 110

⇒ __**116 - 6**__ = 110

**⇒ 110 = 110**

**LHS = RHS**

Option 3) : × and +

Given equation : 106 ÷ 3 × 2 + 70 – 7 = 110

After interchanging the symbols in given equation is as follows : 106 ÷ 3 + 2 × 70 - 7 = 110

⇒ __**106 ÷ 3**__ + 2 × 70 - 7 = 110

⇒ 35.33 + __**2 × 70**__ - 7 = 110

⇒ __**35.33 + 140**__ - 7 = 110

⇒ __**175.33 - 7**__ = 110

⇒ 168.33 ≠ 110

LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) : + and – 

Given equation : 106 ÷ 3 × 2 + 70 – 7 = 110

After interchanging the symbols in given equation is as follows :

106 ÷ 3 × 2 - 70 + 7 = 110

⇒ __**106 ÷ 3**__ × 2 - 70 + 7 = 110

⇒ __**35.33 × 2**__ - 70 + 7 = 110

⇒ __**70.66**__ - 70 __**+ 7**__ = 110

⇒ __**77.66 - 70**__ = 110

⇒ 7.66 ≠ 110

LHS ≠ RHS

Hence, the correct answer is **"– and ÷".**

question: When a number is added to its next number and another number that is 2 times its next number, the sum of these three numbers is 35. Find the number
solution:
Let the number be a.

According to question:

a + (a + 1) + 2 (a + 1) = 35

⇒ a + a + 1 + 2a + 2 = 35

⇒ 4a + 3 = 35

⇒ 4a = 35 - 3

⇒ 4a = 32

⇒ a = 32 ÷ 4

⇒ a = 8

Therefore, the number is 8.

Hence, '**8**' is the correct answer.

question:
If 8 R 10 S 7 T 12 = 75 and 18 R 6 S 8 T 30 = 86, then

24 R 15 S 9 T 35 = ?
solution:
The logic followed here is:

**R means ×, S means +, and T means -**

8 R 10 S 7 T 12 = 75

8 × 10 + 7 - 12 = 80 + 7 - 12 = 75

18 R 6 S 8 T 30 = 86, 

18 × 6 + 8 - 30 = 108 + 8 - 30 = 86

Similarly, 24 R 15 S 9 T 35 = ? 

24 × 15 + 9 - 35 = 360 + 9 - 35 = **334**

Hence, the correct answer is **"334".**

question: If 75 A 30 B 50 C 10 = 40 and 60 A 20 B 80 C 16 = 35, then 60 A 15 B 45 C 5 = ?

The logic followed here is:

**A means -, B means -, C means ÷**

75 A 30 B 50 C 10 = 40

75 - 30 - 50 ÷ 10 = 45 - 5 = 40

60 A 20 B 80 C 16 = 35,

60 - 20 - 80 ÷ 16 = 40 - 5 = 35

Then 60 A 15 B 45 C 5 = ? 

60 - 15 - 45 ÷ 5 = 45 - 9 = **36**

Hence, the correct answer is "36".

question: If the sum of three consecutive odd numbers is 111, what is the largest number?
solution:
Let the three consecutive odd numbers be x, x + 2, and x + 4.

The sum of these numbers is given as 111.

x + (x + 2) + (x + 4) = 111

3x + 6 = 111

3x = 111 − 6

3x = 105

x = 105 ÷ 3

x = 35

First odd number (x) = 35

Second odd number (x + 2) = 37

Third odd number (x + 4) = 39

Comparing the three numbers 35, 37, and 39, the largest number is 39.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 4**”.

question: In a farm, there are cows and hens. The total number of heads is 50 and the total number of legs is 140. How many hens are there?
solution:
Let the number of cows be C and the number of hens be H.

Total heads = 50, so the equation is: C + H = 50 — (i)

Total legs = 140, so the equation is: 4C + 2H = 140 — (ii)

From equation (i), we can express C as: C = 50 − H

Now, substitute the value of C in equation (ii):

4 × (50 − H) + 2H = 140

200 − 4H + 2H = 140

200 − 2H = 140

2H = 200 − 140

2H = 60

H = 60 ÷ 2

H = 30

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 3**”.

question:

What is the respective ratio of present ages of L and M?
solution:
Let the **present age** of **L** be **L** and the **present age** of **M** be **M**.

**5 years ago from the present**

 
 

 Age of **L**
 L − 5
 
 

 Age of **M**
 M − 5
 
 

**
The ratio of their ages was 1 : 3.

(L − 5) / (M − 5) = 1 / 3

3 × (L − 5) = 1 × (M − 5)

3L − 15 = M − 5

**M = 3L − 10** --- (Equation 1)

**After 3 years from the present**

 
 

 Age of **L**
 L + 3
 
 

 Age of **M**
 M + 3
 
 

The ratio of their ages will be 2 : 5.

(L + 3) / (M + 3) = 2 / 5

5 × (L + 3) = 2 × (M + 3)

5L + 15 = 2M + 6

**5L − 2M = −9** --- (Equation 2)

**Solving the Equations:**

Substitute the value of M from Equation 1 into Equation 2:

5L − 2 × (3L − 10) = −9

5L − 6L + 20 = −9

−L + 20 = −9

−L = −29

L = 29

Now, find the value of M using Equation 1:

M = 3 × 29 − 10

M = 87 − 10

M = 77

The **present age** of **L** is 29 and the **present age** of **M** is 77.

The **respective ratio** of their **present ages** (L : M) = **29 : 77**.

Hence, the correct answer is “Option 1**”.

question: In a farm, there are cows and hens. The total number of heads is 50 and the total number of legs is 140. How many cows are there?
solution:
In a farm, **cows** have 4 legs and 1 head each, while **hens** have 2 legs and 1 head each.

Let the number of **cows** be **C** and the number of **hens** be **H**.

C + H = 50 ---- (Equation 1)

(4 × C) + (2 × H) = 140

2C + H = 70 ---- (Equation 2)

Subtract Equation 1 from Equation 2:

(2C + H) − (C + H) = 70 − 50

C = 20

So, the total number of **cows** in the farm is **20**.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”.

 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** 

If all 50 animals were hens, the total legs would be 50 × 2 = 100.

Difference in legs = 140 − 100 = 40.

Difference in legs per animal (Cow vs Hen) = 4 − 2 = 2.

Number of **cows** = 40 ÷ 2 = 20.

The correct answer is **option 1**.

question: Find the difference between the simple interest on ₹6,000 at 12% per annum for 3 years and 2 years.

Given Information:

Principal (P) = ₹6,000

Rate (R) = 12% per annum**
 

Time Period 1 (T1) = 3 years

**Formula:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (Principal × Rate × Time) / 100

SI₁ = (6,000 × 12 × 3) / 100

SI₁ = 60 × 12 × 3

SI₁ = ₹2,160

Now,

SI₂ = (6,000 × 12 × 2) / 100

SI₂ = 60 × 12 × 2

SI₂ = ₹1,440

Difference = SI₁ − SI₂

Difference = 2,160 − 1,440

**Difference = ₹720**

Hence, the correct answer is “Option 3**”.

Difference in SI = 60 × 12 = ₹720

question: The ratio of present ages of two students is 15 : 8. The difference between their ages is 14 years. What is the age of the elder student?

Let the age of the elder student be **15x** and the age of the younger student be **8x**.

Elder Student = 15x

Younger Student = 18x

**According to the question:**

Difference between ages = 15x − 8x

14 = 7x

x = 14 ÷ 7

**x = 2**

Age of the elder student = 15x

Age of the elder student = 15 × 2 = **30 years**

Age of the younger student = 8x

Age of the younger student = 8 × 2 = 16 years

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”.

8x + 8y = 280

(5x + 3y) − (3x + 5y) = 145 &minus

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

⇒ 2412.5 ≠ 187

Option 3) × and -

Given: 136 ÷ 17 + 102 - 3 × 2 = 187

After interchanging the sign we get the;

⇒ __**136 ÷ 17**__ + 102 × 3 - 2 = 187

⇒ 8 + __**102 × 3**__ - 2 = 187

⇒ __**8 + 306**__ -2 = 187

⇒ __**314 - 2**__ = 187

⇒ 312 ≠ 187

⇒ LHS ≠ RHS

Option 4) ÷ and -

Given: 136 ÷ 17 + 102 - 3 × 2 = 187

After interchanging the sign we get the;

⇒ 136 - 17 + __**102 ÷ 3**__ × 2 = 187

⇒ 136 - 17 + 34 × 2 = 187

⇒ 136 - 17 + 68 = 187

⇒ 204 - 17 = 187

⇒ 187 = 187

⇒ LHS = RHS

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

Hence, the correct answer is **"43".**

subject: REAS
question: Two pipes can fill a tank in 12 hours and 18 hours, respectively. A third pipe can empty the tank in 9 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, in how much time will the tank be filled?
solution:
**Given:**

Two pipes can fill a tank in 12 hours and 18 hours.

A third pipe can empty the tank in 9 hours. 

**Formula used:**

Time = Total Capacity ÷ Net Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Let pipes are A, B and C.

Efficiency of **Pipe A** = 36 ÷ 12 = **3 units/hr**

Efficiency of **Pipe B** = 36 ÷ 18 = **2 units/hr**

Efficiency of **Pipe C** = 36 ÷ 9 = **4 units/hr** (Since it empties the tank, its efficiency will be taken as negative).

Net Efficiency = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B − Efficiency of C

Net Efficiency = 3 + 2 − 4 = **1 unit/hr**

Time = Total Capacity ÷ Net Efficiency

Time = 36 ÷ 1 = **36 hours**

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 2**”.

question: Speed of 5 cars A, B, M, S and T is compared. Speed of no two cars is same. Speed of only three cars is more than A. Speed of S is more than atleast four cars. Speed of T is less than M and S. Speed of T is not the least. Speed of M is more than how many cars?
solution:
Given that there are 5 cars A, B, M, S and T with different speeds.

From the clues, we can deduce the following relationships:

1. Speed of only three cars is more than A.

→ A is faster than only one car, so A is the **4th fastest**.

→ _ > _ > _ > A > _

2. Speed of S is more than at least four cars.

→ S is faster than all the other four cars, so **S is the fastest**.

→ S > _ > _ > A > _

3. Speed of T is less than M and S. Speed of T is not the least.

→ Since A is already 4th, T cannot be 5th (least) and cannot be 4th (occupied by A).

→ Therefore, T must be the **3rd fastest**.

→ S > _ > T > A > _

4. M is faster than T.

→ M must occupy the only remaining position above T.

→ **S > M > T > A > B**

Combining all these facts gives the final order from fastest to slowest:

→ **S > M > T > A > B**

Thus, **M is faster than 3 cars (T, A and B).**

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3".**

question:
Sales of 6 companies L, M, N, O, P and Q is compared. Sales of no two companies is same. Sales of L is less than only O. Sales of P is more than only Q. Sales of N is more than M. Which of the following is a correct sequence regarding the sales of these companies?

I. M > Q II. M > L
solution:
Given that the sales of 6 companies L, M, N, O, P and Q are all different.

From the clues, we can deduce the following relationships:

1. Sales of **L** is less than only **O**.

→ Only O has higher sales than L.

→ **O > L > _ > _ > _ > _**

2. Sales of **P** is more than only **Q**.

→ P is the second lowest and Q is the lowest.

→ **_ > _ > _ > L > P > Q**

3. Sales of **N** is more than **M**.

→ **N > M**

4. Since L is already fixed as the second highest, the remaining positions are occupied by O, N and M.

→ Final order becomes:

→ **O > L > N > M > P > Q**

Now check the conclusions:

**I. M > Q** → **True** (M is above Q)

**II. M > L** → **False** (L is above M)

Thus, only conclusion **I** is correct.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

question: Height of 6 persons J, K, L, M, N and O is compared. Height of K is more than only 3 persons. Height of no two persons is same. Height of J is more than M, N and O. Height of J is not maximum. If height of J is 165 cm, then what will be the possible height (in cm) of M?
solution:
Given that there are 6 persons J, K, L, M, N and O with different heights.

From the clues, we can deduce the following relationships:

1. K is taller than only 3 persons.

In a group of 6 people, K is the **3rd tallest**.

→ _ > _ > K > _ > _ > _

2. J is taller than M, N and O.

This means J is taller than exactly these three persons.

→ J > M, N, O

3. J is not the tallest.

Since K is already the 3rd tallest, J cannot be below K (otherwise J would not be taller than M, N and O).

Therefore, J must be the **2nd tallest** and L becomes the tallest.

→ L > J > K > M > N > O

4. J's height is 165 cm.

Since M is shorter than J, M's height must be **less than 165 cm**.

Among the given options, only **160 cm** satisfies this condition.

Thus, the possible arrangement is:

→ **L > J (165 cm) > K > M (160 cm) > N > O**

Hence, the possible height of **M** is **160 cm**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

C is second to the right of G. F is to the immediate right of C. A is third to the left of E. Who is sitting second to the left of A?
solution:
1. Since all persons face the centre: right = counterclockwise, left = clockwise. Fix **G** at pos(1). **C** is second to the right of **G** (counterclockwise): **G(1)** → pos(7) → **C(6)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c2010df80b65e739835e035273ac2e98640aa799439cfc1ec0a2092fb4a58f84.png] 

2. **F** is to the immediate right of **C** (counterclockwise): **C(6)** → **F(5)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e732c79002c5b7f9f43e71cd910259874feca02597b17ecb517c54753936a71d.png] 

3. **A** is third to the left of **E** (clockwise): **E** → skip 2 → **A**. Placing **E** at pos(4) gives **E(4)** → pos(5) → pos(6) → **A(7)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/05f24e39c4bc4a6f6a2067e9c7c9298361a0218e1c8e5c16e9aff181d60e7fc7.png] 

4. **B** is the immediate neighbour of **D** and **E**. This means **B** sits between **D** and **E**. Since **E** is at pos(4), **B** must be at pos(3) and **D** at pos(2).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0258cc4d844feb42a31283ab88ce2efaa891c76dd5c8f086247b473df80b0d7c.png] 

The final arrangement is **G(1)**, **D(2)**, **B(3)**, **E(4)**, **F(5)**, **C(6)**, **A(7)** in clockwise order. To find the person sitting second to the left of **A**, move clockwise from **A(7)**: **A(7)** → **G(1)** (first left) → **D(2)** (second left). Thus, **D** sits second to the left of **A**.

 

Hence, the correct answer is **'Option 1'**.

C is fourth to the left of G. B is the immediate neighbour of F and G. D is not the immediate neighbour of C. A is second to the left of B. What is the position of E with respect to F?
solution:
1. Since all persons face **opposite to the centre**: **Right = Clockwise**, **Left = Counterclockwise**. Fix **G** at pos(1). **F** is fifth to the right of **G** (clockwise): G(1) → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → **F(6)**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d3a67215060a4519ad3e7be34fbd80dd460def29595ad8fbae662b0ded47898c.png] 
2. **C** is fourth to the left of **G** (counterclockwise): G(1) → 7 → 6 → 5 → **C(4)**. **B** is an immediate neighbour of **F** and **G**; the only position between them is pos(7), so **B** is at **pos(7)**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7f218122ab7091fd43aafd09106f360061b63a2b8d3a90825a420f0036103656.png] 
3. **A** is second to the left of **B** (counterclockwise): B(7) → 6 → **A(5)**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/90c0f2ef619f53e00b715e8d806742e0805c4fa58ee0903e91e9fc60658c5b8d.png] 
4. **D** is not an immediate neighbour of **C**(4). Neighbours of 4 are pos(3) and pos(5). Since pos(5) is occupied by **A**, **D** cannot be at 3. Thus, **D** must be at **pos(2)**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/05c882ff3625e848f4895d0526fedab9a487ba708169be94840c8defb8fdaa0d.png] 
5. The remaining position, **pos(3)**, is filled by **E**. Final arrangement: **G(1)**, **D(2)**, **E(3)**, **C(4)**, **A(5)**, **F(6)**, **B(7)**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ce74b142607557c5d53b0663d60d859c9902e65b1ab177dee1b867902db33505.png] 
Position of **E** with respect to **F**: Starting at **F(6)** and moving left (counterclockwise direction for outward-facing seats): 6 → 5(A) → 4(C) → **3(E)**. Thus, **E** is **third to the left** of **F**.

Hence, the correct answer is **'Option 1'**.

question: A certain number of persons are standing in a row facing south. Q is standing second from the right end of the row. S is standing seventh to the left of M. Only one person stand between S and O, when counted towards right of S. Only two persons stand between Q and M. O is fourth to the right of R. Who among the following person stands eight to the right of O?
solution:
According to the given information, a certain number of persons are facing **south** in a row. In a south-facing arrangement, the **right** direction is towards our left and the **left** direction is towards our right.

**Step-by-step derivation:**

**1) Q is standing second from the right end of the row:**

If we number the positions starting from the **right end** as 1, then **Q** is at position 2.

**2) Only two persons stand between Q and M:**

Since **Q** is at position 2, there are two positions (3 and 4) between them, making **M** at position 5.

**3) S is standing seventh to the left of M:**

Facing south, the left direction moves towards higher position numbers. So, **S** is at position 5 + 7 = 12.

**4) Only one person stands between S and O, when counted towards the right of S:**

The right direction moves towards lower position numbers. One person between position 12 (S) and **O** means **O** is at position 10 (with position 11 being the person between them).

**5) O is fourth to the right of R:**

If **O** is to the right of **R**, then **R** must be to the left of **O** (higher number position). **R** is at position 10 + 4 = 14.

**The arrangement can be summarized in the following table:**

Now, we need to find who stands **eighth to the right of O**:

Position of **O** = 10

Counting 8 positions towards the right (lower numbers): 10 − 8 = 2

At position 2, the person standing is **Q**.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1".**

**Second Letter:** The letters decrease by 2 in alphabetical order.

A − 2 = Y

Y − 2 = W

**W − 2 = U**

U − 2 = S

**Third Letter:** The letters decrease by 3 in alphabetical order.

L − 3 = I

I − 3 = F

**F − 3 = C**

C − 3 = Z

**Positional values for the missing term letters (JUC):**

 **J**
 **U**
 **C**

 10
 21
 3

**2) Logic for the Numbers:**

The numbers follow a **geometric progression** where each number is multiplied by a constant factor of **1.5**.

5 × 1.5 = 7.5

7.5 × 1.5 = 11.25

**11.25 × 1.5 = 16.875**

16.875 × 1.5 = 25.3125

Combining the letters and the number, the missing term is **JUC16.875**.

The correct answer is **option 2**</p

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 1".

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 3**”.

subject: REAS
question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully and decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All scientists working in Japan are talented.

Some Chinese scientists are working in Japan.

**Conclusions:**

I. No Chinese scientist is talented.

II. Some talented Chinese scientists are working in Japan.

III. All talented scientists are Japanese.

IV. Some Chinese scientists are talented.

options.text: Only conclusion III and IV follow
Only conclusion II and IV follow.

solution:
According to the given statements,

***Conclusion I:*** This does not follow, because it is mentioned in the statement that all the scientists working in Japan are talented, but it is not mentioned only Japanese people are talented.

***Conclusion II: ***This follow, because it is mentioned in the second statement that some Chinese scientists are also working in Japan.

***Conclusion III:*** This does not follow, because it is not mentioned in the statement that only Japanese are talented.

***Conclusion IV: ***This follows because some Chinese scientists are working in Japan.

Hence,** “only conclusion II and IV” follow.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87c1a28e731fadd9279228c1cea2f8e988a3f790bf9ccc89c9b0f02c423b1609.png] 

 
• If there are two or more sentences that are used to frame a statement, then, the sentences must be interrelated, and mutual contradiction should be there.
 
• **Do not look for truthful notions. The information provided in the statement is the only requirement for a student to answer the question. No assumptions must be made.**
 
• Read the statement carefully and look for keywords that are common between the statement and the conclusions
 
• If there is more than one conclusion that is applicable to the statement, students must ensure that the conclusions they opt for have some relation with each other.
